description: Unauthorized Access to Cloud Credentials An attacker could exploit overly permissive IAM roles or misconfigured secrets access policies to retrieve cloud credentials stored in Secrets Manager. A compromised Lambda function with excessive permissions could access Secrets Manager and retrieve credentials for all cloud providers, leading to unauthorized access across multiple cloud environments.
references: recommendation: Implement strict IAM policies following the principle of least privilege
recommendation: Implement AWS Organizations SCPs as recommended by security engineer

description: Sensitive Cost Data Exposure via S3 Misconfigured S3 bucket policies or inadequate access controls could allow unauthorized access to sensitive cost data stored in the buckets. An attacker could exploit overly permissive bucket policies to access or modify cost data, potentially leading to data leakage or manipulation of cost reports.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement comprehensive S3 bucket security controls
recommendation: Implement data classification and handling controls

description: API Gateway Authentication Bypass Insufficient API Gateway authentication configuration or vulnerabilities in the authentication mechanism could allow unauthorized access to the API endpoints. An attacker could forge or manipulate authentication tokens to gain unauthorized access to cost management APIs.
references: recommendation: Implement robust API Gateway authentication
recommendation: Implement API request throttling and monitoring

description: DynamoDB Data Manipulation Overly permissive IAM policies or compromised Lambda functions could allow unauthorized modification of cost data in DynamoDB. An attacker with access to a compromised Lambda function could modify cost data to hide resource usage or manipulate billing information.
references: recommendation: Implement strict DynamoDB access controls

description: EventBridge Rule Manipulation Attackers with IAM permissions could modify EventBridge rules to disrupt cost data collection timing or frequency. An attacker could modify scheduling rules to prevent cost data collection or overwhelm the system with too frequent collections.
